subject: math
explanation:
Why Do We Need Standard Form?
Imagine writing:
299,792,458
This is the speed of light in metres per second.
Easy to make mistakes while reading.
Now imagine:
0.000000000167
This is also difficult to read.
Scientists needed a simpler method.
So they invented:
Standard Form

What Is Standard Form?

 A number is written as:
𝑎 × 10𝑛
where:
•

1 ≤ 𝑎 < 10

•

𝑛is an integer

Example 1
3000
Move decimal:
3000.0
↓
3.0
Moved:
3 places
Therefore:
3000 = 3 × 103

Example 2
45000
45000 = 4.5 × 104

Example 3
0.004
Move decimal:
0.004
↓

 4
Moved:
3 places right
Therefore:
0.004 = 4 × 10−3

Example 4
0.00056
0.00056 = 5.6 × 10−4

Shortcut
Large Numbers
Move decimal LEFT
Exponent becomes POSITIVE

Small Numbers
Move decimal RIGHT
Exponent becomes NEGATIVE

sections.heading: 5. MISCONCEPTIONS
sections.content:
Misconception 1

35 × 104
is standard form.
Wrong.
First number must be between 1 and 10.

Misconception 2
Negative exponent means negative number.
Wrong.
5 × 10−3
is positive.

Misconception 3
Standard form changes value.
Wrong.
Only representation changes.
Value remains exactly same.

Misconception 4
Standard form is used only in science.

 Wrong.
Used in:
•

banking

•

computers

•

engineering

•

astronomy

•

statistics

sections.heading: 7. QUIZ
sections.content:
Q1
Write:
5000
in standard form.
A.
5 × 103
B.
50 × 102
C.
500 × 10

Answer: A

Q2
Write:
0.0004
in standard form.
A.

 4 × 10−4
B.
4 × 10−3
C.
4 × 104

Answer: A

Q3
Which number is in standard form?
A.
35 × 104
B.
3.5 × 105
C.
350 × 103

Answer: B

Q4
For large numbers, exponent is usually:
A. Negative
B. Positive
C. Zero
Answer: B

 Q5
For very small numbers, exponent is usually:
A. Positive
B. Negative
C. One
Answer: B

Q6
Which field heavily uses standard form?
A. Astronomy
B. Biology
C. Engineering
D. All of these
Answer: D

Q7
Why was standard form invented?
A. To make numbers longer
B. To simplify very large and very small numbers
C. To avoid calculations
D. None
Answer: B
